questions.text: Fall protection systems (guardrails, harnesses, or nets) are in place for all work at 6+ feet.
A written fall protection plan is on file for the job site.
Scaffolding is erected and inspected by a documented competent person.
Guardrails and toe boards are installed on all scaffold platforms above 10 feet.
Scaffold load ratings are documented and not exceeded.
A written Hazard Communication (HazCom) program is on file.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are accessible on-site for every chemical present.
All temporary wiring and outlets are protected with GFCI.
Electrical panels and temporary power are inspected before use.
Trenches 5+ feet deep are protected by shoring, sloping, or a trench box.
Daily trench inspections are documented by a competent person.
An OSHA 300 Log is maintained and available on-site (required at 11+ employees).
The OSHA 300A annual summary is posted each year from February 1 through April 30.
Ladders are inspected and properly secured before use.
Required PPE (hard hats, eye protection) is provided and worn.
A heat illness prevention plan is in place for outdoor crews.
Toolbox talks / safety training sessions are documented at regular intervals.
An emergency action plan is posted and communicated to all workers.
The contractor holds an active, unrestricted CILB license in the operating entity's name.
All work performed falls within the license category scope (Certified vs. Registered).
County/local registration is current where Registered-category work occurs.
14 hours of continuing education per biennium are complete, including the required safety, business practices, workers' comp, and wind mitigation hours.
Financial responsibility documentation (net worth, credit history) is current for renewal.
The qualifying agent is actively and directly supervising operations.
A plan exists to replace the qualifying agent within 60 days if they depart.
All permits are pulled by a properly licensed individual.
No unlicensed-activity findings or pending DBPR disciplinary action exist.
The business name/DBA in use matches the name on file with DBPR.
A certificate of insurance on file matches license requirements.
The license renewal deadline is tracked and has not lapsed.
Every subcontractor engaged is verified as properly licensed before work begins.
No employees perform work requiring a license they do not individually hold.
Advertising and marketing materials display the license number as required.
Workers' compensation coverage is in force for all employees (1+ employee threshold).
An owner exemption is filed correctly if the owner claims exempt status.
Policy class codes match the work actually performed.
No open stop-work order exists from the Florida Division of Workers' Compensation.
A certificate of insurance is requested and verified for every subcontractor before they start work.
Subcontractor COIs are kept on file and checked for current expiration.
Annual payroll audit records are reconciled against policy class codes.
No history of misclassifying employees as 1099 subcontractors to avoid coverage.
Policy premium is current with no lapses in coverage.
A job-site injury reporting procedure is documented and communicated to workers.
A return-to-work / modified duty policy exists.
The experience modification rate (EMR) is reviewed annually.
Coverage limits are adequate for project size and GC requirements.
Records are retained for the 2-year lookback period insurers/DWC may audit.
EPA RRP firm certification is current for any work on pre-1978 buildings.
All renovators performing RRP work are individually certified/trained.
Lead-safe containment practices (plastic sheeting, dust control) are documented on RRP jobs.
Pre-renovation lead disclosure/notification is provided to occupants.
A SWPPP is prepared for any site disturbing 1+ acre.
An NPDES permit is obtained through FDEP before land-disturbing activity begins.
Erosion/sediment controls are inspected and maintained per the SWPPP schedule.
An asbestos inspection is completed before demolition or renovation of commercial structures.
NESHAP notification is filed with the appropriate agency before demolition.
Hazardous waste (paint, solvents, adhesives) is disposed of per EPA/FDEP requirements.
A spill response plan/kit is available on job sites using hazardous materials.
Underground storage tank removal, where applicable, is permitted and documented.
Wetlands/environmental resource permits are obtained where required.
Dust/air quality controls are in place for demolition work.
All permitted work complies with the current Florida Building Code edition.
Building plans reflect the current code cycle, not a superseded edition.
HVHZ product approvals (NOA) are on file for materials used in Miami-Dade/Broward.
Roofing/window/door products match approved NOA listings for the region.
Wind-load calculations are documented for HVHZ projects.
Energy code compliance (insulation, HVAC, fenestration) is documented at permit.
Required inspections are scheduled and passed at each construction milestone.
As-built plans are retained and match the permitted scope.
No open or expired permits exist on active or recently completed jobs.
Flood zone / elevation certificate requirements are met where applicable.
Impact-resistant or shutter compliance is verified for hurricane-zone openings.
Product approval documentation is available for client/inspector review.
Code-required accessibility (ADA) provisions are met on commercial work.
Worker classification (employee vs. 1099) is reviewed against the IRS common-law test.
E-Verify enrollment is current where required (private employers 25+ employees, or public contractors).
E-Verify checks are completed and documented for all new hires subject to the requirement.
No open misclassification disputes exist with the IRS or Florida Department of Revenue.
Sales tax on building materials is collected/remitted correctly as the end consumer.
Florida Department of Revenue registration is current.
Payroll tax withholding and filings are current (federal and state).
1099s are issued correctly and on time for legitimate subcontractors.
I-9 forms are completed and retained for all employees.
No unpaid wage claims or Department of Labor complaints are pending.
Overtime is calculated correctly per FLSA for non-exempt employees.
Independent contractor agreements are in writing and consistent with the actual working relationship.
Records are retained per IRS/DOR statute of limitations for audits.
